newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits little changed ahead of ECI.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits little changed ahead of ECI.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were little changed in lacklustre trade with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S fourth quarter employment cost index (ECI) data, dealers said on Tuesday.
They said the market is also waiting for tonight's issue of the U.S. January consumer confidence index figures.
The employment cost index for the fourth quarter is forecast to show an increase of 0.9 percent compared with a 0.6 percent gain reported in the third quarter.
The January consumer confidence index is expected to slip to 112.0 percent against December's 113.8 percent.

"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning on some position adjustments. All eyes are on tonight's release of the (fourth quarter) employment cost index and (January) consumer confidence index figures," a local dealer said.
"But I don't think there will be much impact as the numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared their positions for the day," he said.
"Some people are also waiting for Wednesday's release of the (December) durable goods and Thursday's issue of the weekly jobless claims data, for fresh clues to market direction," he added.
In day-to-day rates, Tuesday/Wednesday eased 1/16 percentage point to 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent.
Wednesday/Thursday and week-fixed were unchanged from Monday's common 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent, respectively.

Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged at 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent, four-months unchanged at 5-9/16 5-7/16, six-months unchanged at 5-11/16 5-9/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 5-15/16 5-13/16 percent.
